analysis:
Examined docs/threat-model.yaml BASE lines 898–1873 against the canonical index and supplied change ranges. These excerpts are unchanged surrounding evidence, not implementation changes. They cover cancellation, process-scoped encryption keys, weight integrity, binary/runtime protections, GPU residuals, idle unloading, encrypted cache isolation/storage, legacy attestation and continuity, watchdog recovery, and privileged fan-helper controls. Existing limitations and accepted risks are not PR regressions.
The patch introduces serving-availability asset A-018 and local add-on socket boundary TB-012 (HEAD lines 232–241 and 811 onward); its header also announces T-059. This adds a same-user, separately signed add-on coordination contract affecting inference admission, resident models, and heartbeat/busy routing state. The supplied boundary patch is truncated, and these units contain neither the full new definitions nor hold implementation, so no missing authentication or lease control is established here.
Integration should reconcile the new hold behavior with T-010 cancellation, T-029 unloading, T-053 authorization lifetime, and T-047 fan-lease shutdown semantics. Examine ProviderCore/Addon/ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift and the socket/lease/machine-lock implementation in the relevant source batches, including signature enforcement, stale-hold recovery, in-flight work, and busy-state publication. Coordinator interpretation of busy fields remains an explicitly external contract, not evidence of a routing regression. No supported finding arises from these unchanged BASE excerpts; material new-boundary behavior remains unresolved in this local scope.
